description: Team Nexarc is building a 3D web tool that matches Earth locations to planned Moon base and Mars sites using NASA/USGS open data (slope, elevation, temperature, terrain roughness). We are CSE students from DSU Bengaluru. Skills: Next.js, React, Three.js, GSAP, Tailwind, Supabase, Gemini API. Looking for: data analysis/GIS (Python), geospatial or planetary science interest, UI/UX designer, and someone good at pitching. Join us to build a winning, demo-ready project!
summary:
TERRALIGN is an interactive planetary analogue research platform designed to help explore how Earth's landscapes can serve as reference environments for lunar and Martian exploration. It combines an interactive 3D Earth globe, mission-specific analogue discovery, side-by-side 3D terrain comparison, solar-grazing illumination, and a six-axis Analog Reality Gap (ARG) assessment.

The platform brings together references from NASA LRO LOLA, NASA MGS MOLA, NASA SRTM, and USGS 3DEP elevation datasets to support terrain exploration and scientific context. Users can compare landscape characteristics, inspect elevation profiles, and explore model-assessed similarities and differences between terrestrial and planetary environments.

TERRALIGN presents analytical indicators as decision-support tools rather than scientific ground truth. Its goal is to make planetary analogue exploration more visual, accessible, and useful for research planning.
details:
TERRALIGN is a web-based planetary analogue research and decision-support platform that helps researchers explore how Earth's landscapes can serve as reference environments for lunar and Martian exploration.

Users can explore terrestrial analogue locations, switch between Earth, Moon, and Mars views, compare terrain through dual 3D WebGL viewports, inspect elevation profiles, and examine terrain similarities and differences using the Analog Reality Gap (ARG) assessment. Solar-grazing illumination helps visualize surface features under low-angle lighting. The platform also includes a mission-oriented discovery workflow, portfolio analysis, dataset uploads, and an AI Research Assistant.

The project uses scientific references from NASA LRO LOLA, NASA MGS MOLA, NASA SRTM, and USGS 3DEP. Data provenance and limitations are considered important: some planetary terrain representations use calibrated or static reference data, and ARG scores are model-assessed indicators rather than validated scientific measurements.

The application was developed using Next.js, React, TypeScript, Three.js, WebGL, Tailwind CSS, and Node.js. Its goal is to make planetary analogue exploration more visual, accessible, and useful for research planning while helping users understand uncertainty before applying Earth-based observations to other worlds.
